bull.b: GM currently generates meaningful free cash flow (~$13.4B TTM) and robust operating cash (~$23.2B TTM). That durable cash generation supports continued capex, EV transition spending, dividend/share buybacks and balance-sheet flexibility, enabling multi-year strategic investment despite past volatility.

bull.t: North America margin recovery and pickup leadership
bull.b: North America returned to target margins (8.6% adj. EBIT) while maintaining dominant full-size pickup share (>42%). This product-market strength and scale in high-margin trucks provides structural pricing power and margin resilience, underpinning sustained profitability in the region over the medium term.

Deferred revenue and subscription growth (deferred revenue ~$6.3B; Q2 digital revenue $800M; ~1M new subscriptions) point to expanding high-margin, recurring revenue streams. Over 2–6 months this increases revenue visibility, improves lifetime customer value and diversifies profit drivers beyond vehicle sales.

bear.b: Leverage near ~2.0x combined with sharply reduced margins and ROE (~4% TTM) limits financial flexibility. For a cyclical automaker, higher debt increases vulnerability to demand shocks, constrains incremental investment capacity, and raises the hurdle for sustained returns during downturns.

Cumulative EV restructuring charges (~$10.9B, ~$7.2B cash impact) represent a substantial, multi-year drag on capital and earnings. Such write-downs reflect execution and capacity adjustments that can suppress returns and absorb cash that might otherwise fund growth or improve margins until EV profitability normalizes.

bear.t: Material tariff, commodity and onshoring cost pressures
bear.b: Multi-billion-dollar structural cost headwinds from tariffs, commodities/DRAM and planned onshoring (~$2.5–$3.5B tariffs; $1.5–$2.0B commodity; $1.0–$1.5B onshoring) compress margins and raise break-even requirements. These persistent input and policy-driven costs can offset margin gains unless mitigated by pricing or efficiency gains.
